groups.sentence: Everyone must submit AI tools for IT or governance review and get approval before acquiring or using them, even free ones.
Administrators establish a process to review and approve AI tools and vendors for security, privacy, risk and compliance before adoption.
Administrators ensure AI vendor contracts include data protection, privacy and security terms, and that vendors disclose their AI use.
IT or security offices review AI tools for security, privacy, legal and accessibility standards before approval.
Everyone must follow the university's standard procurement process for AI purchases and subscriptions.
Instructors must get an AI tool reviewed or approved by IT before requiring it in a course or using it with student work.
Everyone may submit requests for new AI tools to be reviewed or integrated.
Staff must obtain approval through standard contracting and procurement before acquiring AI tools.
Everyone may use university information with AI tools only if the tool is approved for that data type and use.
Administrators review approved AI tools again periodically or when they change.
The university is continuing to evaluate AI tools, and current agreements and detection tools have limits.
Administrators may block, restrict or prohibit unauthorized or risky AI tools.
Vendors and third parties must not use university data to train or improve AI models unless explicitly authorized.
Vendor contracts exist or restrict training on university data, and data entered into some AI products is retained.
The university publishes lists of approved, prohibited or reviewed AI tools.
Administrators do not authorize licensing or sharing university data or intellectual property externally for AI purposes, and AI agreements need General Counsel review.
